description: issue #775 (review gate): `every :p` where `:p` is a RECORD -- the twin of `wait/wait-non-number-dict-type-error`, completing `params.actual` across every `OLTypeName` outside `number`/`word` alongside the list, boolean, and turtle fixtures. Before them the whole corpus (`wait`, `every`, `repeat`, `random`) pinned `actual` as only `number` or `word`, so an implementation could report anything at all for a record and still pass -- confirmed by mutation. `spec/error-model.md` requires an `ol-type` to "name the expected learner concept, such as number, word, list, dict, record, or boolean", so calling a record a word would violate a MUST. The record's CONTENTS are genuinely compared: the harness unwraps an `OLRecord` into a plain field->value object before deep-comparing, and the reserved `__type` key opts in to asserting WHICH struct type it is (`tests/conformance/README.md`, "Dict/record contents" and "Record struct type") -- both are used here, so a `point`-shaped stand-in or a record with different field values fails. Needs the Data profile only to CONSTRUCT the value; the check under test is the Interaction one. The `struct` declaration and the assignment each emit their own instruction event first; the check fails BEFORE registration, so no `primitive` event is emitted and no handler is registered, and the span covers just the count argument.
